newsitem.title: USA: US home mortgage interest rates inch down in week.
newsitem.headline: US home mortgage interest rates inch down in week.

text.p: Average interest rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages inched down in the week ending October 25 from the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
Freddie Mac said 30-year mortgages averaged 7.86 percent, down two basis points from 7.88 percent last week.
Fifteen-year loans dipped by the same number of basis points to 7.37 percent from 7.39 percent.
Adjustable rate mortgages fell to an average 5.57 percent from 5.62 percent in the week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.45 percent, the 15-year 7.01 percent, and the ARM 5.73 percent.
"Consumer and price data released over the last two weeks confirm that inflation remains stable," Frank Nothaft, deputy chief economist for Freddie Mac, said.
"Consequently, mortgage rates have stayed within a narrow 7-3/4 percent to 8-3/4 percent band since March of this year," Nothaft added.
Last week the Labor Department said that U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in September, while real earnings rose 0.8 percent.
On Friday the National Association of Realtors will issue U.S. September existing home sales data.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, up from 1.7 percent last week. They charged 1.5 percent on ARM loans, up also from 1.4 percent the previous week.
